title: Ship It — Deployment, Monitoring & Your Prediction Story
subtitle: Persist the pipeline, track it, put a front end on it, watch it drift, know the rules — then the night the course was built for: your prediction stories, presented

objectives.title: Ship a Pipeline, Not a Model
objectives.description: joblib.dump the whole fitted Pipeline — preprocessing and all — so scoring a new customer is one line and the encoder can't drift from the model.

objectives.title: Track, Serve, and Monitor
objectives.description: MLflow to record every experiment, Gradio to give a model a face in ten lines, Evidently to detect when the data feeding the model no longer looks like the data that trained it.

objectives.title: Know the Rules of the Road
objectives.description: The EU AI Act's risk tiers and AI-literacy duty, the deferred high-risk deadlines for credit and hiring, and the US state laws (Colorado, Jan 2027) requiring explanation and human review for consequential automated decisions.

objectives.title: Tell a Prediction Story
objectives.description: Question, data, model, honest evaluation, decision with a number, trust story. Eight minutes, one narrative — the skill the whole semester was building toward.

agenda.title: From Notebook to Production: Persist the Pipeline
agenda.description: The Telco pipeline, fitted, saved with joblib, loaded in a fresh process, scoring a new customer from a dict. Version the file, record the scikit-learn version, and never save the model without its preprocessing.
bulletPoints: A model file without its ColumnTransformer is a model that will silently mis-score the first unseen category
Reproducibility checklist: random_state, library versions, data snapshot, the exact training query

agenda.title: Track It With MLflow, Serve It With Gradio
agenda.description: mlflow.start_run, log_params, log_metrics, log_model — the experiment log that replaces 'final_v3_REAL.ipynb'. Then gradio.Interface around predict_proba: a working web demo of the churn model from inside Colab in ten lines, shareable by link.
bulletPoints: MLflow 3 tracks classical experiments and LLM traces in one UI
A Gradio demo is the fastest way to let a business owner poke at a model and find its failure modes

agenda.title: Monitor It: Drift, Decay, and the Rules
agenda.description: Models rot. Evidently compares this month's input distributions to the training data and flags drift; label delay means you watch the inputs before you can watch the accuracy. Then one slide on the law: EU AI Act risk tiers and the AI-literacy duty in force since 2025, high-risk obligations for credit scoring and hiring now due Dec 2027, and Colorado's SB 26-189 rules for consequential decisions from Jan 2027.
bulletPoints: Watch input drift weekly, outcome metrics when labels arrive, and set a retraining trigger before launch
If your model touches credit, hiring, insurance, or health, it is in scope somewhere: explanation, human review, and documentation are the direction of travel

agenda.title: Final Presentations, Block 1
agenda.description: Six teams, eight minutes each plus two for questions. The question, the data, the model, the honest evaluation, the decision with a number, the trust story. The audience asks the executive's questions: why this prediction? how sure? what if it's wrong?
bulletPoints: Timekeeper is strict at 8:00 — practice with a clock
Every listener writes one sentence per team: the number they remember

agenda.title: Final Presentations, Block 2
agenda.description: The remaining teams. Same format, same questions, same clock.
bulletPoints: Notebooks and memos were due last night; presentations are graded on the story, not the slides
Listeners' one-sentence notes go in the box for the Signal Award vote

agenda.title: The Signal Award & Closing
agenda.description: The class votes for the project that best found the signal: a real question, an honest model, a decision that changed because of it, and a number attached. Then the last word: you can now take any business question about the future, frame it, model it, evaluate it honestly, and turn it into a decision. That is the skill. Use it well.
bulletPoints: Grades posted within a week; the course site stays up — the notebooks are yours
ISOM 839 (Prescriptive Analytics) picks up where the decision memo ends: from prediction to optimization

activities.title: Save It, Serve It, Watch It
activities.description: Take the Telco churn pipeline from Session 6 (with its tuned threshold). Persist it, reload it in a clean state, score a single new customer, wrap it in a Gradio demo, and run a drift report against a deliberately shifted sample.

steps.title: Persist the whole pipeline
steps.description: joblib.dump(model, 'churn_pipeline_v1.joblib'). Record sklearn.__version__ and the training date in a small JSON next to it.

steps.title: Reload and score one customer
steps.description: In a fresh cell: load, build a one-row DataFrame from a dict, predict_proba. This is what the production service will do.

steps.title: Give it a face
steps.description: gr.Interface with sliders for tenure and monthly charges and dropdowns for contract, internet service, payment method → churn probability and the recommended action at the tuned threshold.

steps.title: Check for drift
steps.description: Shift the test set (e.g., tenure × 0.6, more month-to-month contracts) and run an Evidently DataDriftPreset report comparing it to the training data. Read which columns drifted.

codeBlock.code:
import joblib, json, sklearn, pandas as pd
import gradio as gr

# 1) persist the fitted Pipeline (preprocessing + model), plus metadata
joblib.dump(model, 'churn_pipeline_v1.joblib')
json.dump({'sklearn': sklearn.__version__, 'threshold': 0.12, 'trained': '2026-12-14'}, open('churn_pipeline_v1.json', 'w'))

# 2) reload in a clean state and score one customer
pipe = joblib.load('churn_pipeline_v1.joblib')
meta = json.load(open('churn_pipeline_v1.json'))
def score(tenure, monthly, contract, internet, payment):
    row = pd.DataFrame([{'tenure': tenure, 'MonthlyCharges': monthly, 'Contract': contract,
                         'InternetService': internet, 'PaymentMethod': payment}])
    p = float(pipe.predict_proba(row)[0, 1])
    return f'{p:.1%} churn risk — ' + ('SEND RETENTION OFFER' if p >= meta['threshold'] else 'no action')

# 3) a web demo in one call (share=True gives a public link from Colab)
gr.Interface(score,
    inputs=[gr.Slider(0, 72, 12, label='Tenure (months)'), gr.Slider(18, 120, 70, label='Monthly charges'),
            gr.Dropdown(['Month-to-month', 'One year', 'Two year'], value='Month-to-month', label='Contract'),
            gr.Dropdown(['DSL', 'Fiber optic', 'No'], value='Fiber optic', label='Internet'),
            gr.Dropdown(['Electronic check', 'Mailed check', 'Bank transfer (automatic)', 'Credit card (automatic)'], value='Electronic check', label='Payment')],
    outputs='text', title='Telco churn — ISOM 835').launch(share=True)

activities.discussionNote: Notice what the demo exposes in thirty seconds that a notebook never would: a business owner drags tenure to 70 months on a month-to-month contract and asks why the risk is still 20%. That question — why? — is Session 9's SHAP waterfall, and the honest answer might be 'the model has seen very few such customers,' which is Session 9's conformal set saying {both}. Shipping is where the trust layer stops being theory.

takeaways.text: Ship the pipeline, not the model. Persist preprocessing and estimator together, record versions and thresholds, and score new rows exactly the way training rows were built.

Models rot. Track experiments, monitor input drift before labels arrive, set a retraining trigger before launch — and know that credit, hiring, insurance, and health models now come with explanation and human-review obligations.
You can now take any business question about the future, frame it, model it in Python, evaluate it honestly, and turn it into a decision with a number attached. That was the promise. Find the signal.

homework.label: After the Finale

If you want to keep going: ISOM 839 (Prescriptive Analytics) turns predictions into optimal decisions; the Kaggle Favorita and Home Credit competitions are excellent next problems; and the Inria scikit-learn MOOC and ISLP labs will deepen everything we did. Thank you for a wonderful semester.
